bottom_line: In RALES, spironolactone vs placebo reduced death from any cause (relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001).
implications: In this population (1663 patients) with severe heart failure, spironolactone compared with placebo was associated with a lower risk of death from any cause (relative risk 0.70; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001) and fewer hospitalizations for worsening heart failure (relative risk 0.65; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.77; P<0.001). These numbers support benefit on mortality and morbidity during a mean follow-up of 24 months, while also showing increased gynecomastia/breast pain in men (10% vs 1%) and low serious hyperkalemia (1% vs 2%).

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in severe heart failure comparing spironolactone 25 mg daily vs placebo.
major_points.quote: After the initial evaluation, patients were randomly assigned in a double-blind fashion to receive either 25 mg of spironolactone (Aldactone, Searle, Skokie, Ill.) once daily or a matching placebo.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was death from any cause and analysis was intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote: The primary end point of the study was death from any cause.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early after interim analysis showed efficacy; mean follow-up 24 months.
major_points.quote: the trial was stopped on August 24, 1998, after a mean follow-up of 24 months, on the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring board.

major_points.text: Hospitalization for worsening heart failure was reduced (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.54–0.77; P<0.001).
Gynecomastia or breast pain in men was more frequent with spironolactone (10% vs 1%; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: Gynecomastia or breast pain was reported by 10 percent of the men in the spironolactone group and 1 percent of the men in the placebo group (P<0.001)

major_points.text: Serious hyperkalemia was uncommon and similar between groups (1% vs 2%).

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class IV heart failure within the six months before enrollment and NYHA class III or IV at enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible for enrollment if they had had New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV heart failure within the six months before enrollment and were in NYHA class III or IV at the time of enrollment

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosis of heart failure at least six weeks before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: had been given a diagnosis of heart failure at least six weeks before enrollment

inclusion_criteria.text: Treated with an ACE inhibitor (if tolerated) and a loop diuretic.
inclusion_criteria.quote: were being treated with an ACE inhibitor (if tolerated) and a loop diuretic

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction no more than 35 percent within six months before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: had a left ventricular ejection fraction of no more than 35 percent within the six months before enrollment

exclusion_criteria.text: Primary operable valvular heart disease (other than mitral or tricuspid regurgitation with clinical symptoms due to LV systolic HF).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded from the study if they had primary operable valvular heart disease (other than mitral or tricuspid regurgitation with clinical symptoms due to left ventricular systolic heart failure)

exclusion_criteria.text: Prior heart transplantation or awaiting the procedure.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who had undergone heart transplantation or were awaiting the procedure were also ineligible.

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum creatinine concentration more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (221 µmol per liter).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Other criteria for exclusion were a serum creatinine concentration of more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (221 µmol per liter)

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum potassium concentration more than 5.0 mmol per liter.
exclusion_criteria.quote: and a serum potassium concentration of more than 5.0 mmol per liter.

criticisms.text: Findings may not apply to less severe heart failure; further prospective study is stated as needed.
criticisms.quote: The effectiveness and risks of treatment with spironolactone in patients at lower risk than those in our study, such as those with less severe heart failure, will require further prospective study.
